s1.syndrome_frame: Recurrent respiratory episodes with chronic infection and metabolic disturbances in a young patient
salient_findings: Frequent respiratory episodes during first year of life
Pseudo-Bartter's syndrome with hypochloremia, hyponatremia, hypokalemia, and metabolic alkalosis
Chronic bacterial presence in oropharyngeal samples
key_facts: Male patient born in 2013
Initial sweat tests were uncertain (42-60 mmol/l)
Developed Pseudo-Bartter's syndrome at 8-10 months
Genetic testing at 12 months revealed F508del/3849 + 10kbC-T mutation
Regular oropharyngeal samples showed bacterial presence from 2015 to 2018
No significant aggravation on physical examination from 2015 to 2022
Blood chemistry had no significant deviations
Vitamin D level was within normal range
Regular sputum microbiological examinations from 2014 to 2022
Computer tomography confirmed inflammatory alteration of the paranasal sinuses
Lung computer tomography showed no signs of damage

shortlist.label: Cystic Fibrosis
shortlist.why_kept: Genetic testing revealed F508del/3849 + 10kbC-T mutation, consistent with Cystic Fibrosis

shortlist.label: Pseudo-Bartter Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Patient developed Pseudo-Bartter's syndrome at 8-10 months, with hypochloremia, hyponatremia, hypokalemia, and metabolic alkalosis

shortlist.label: Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia
shortlist.why_kept: Recurrent respiratory episodes and chronic infection, which are common features of Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia

shortlist.label: Bronchiectasis
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic infection and recurrent respiratory episodes, which can lead to bronchiectasis

shortlist.label: Shwachman-Diamond Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's presentation with recurrent respiratory episodes, pancreatic insufficiency is not mentioned but the syndrome is a rare cause of similar symptoms

raw.rationale: The patient's genetic testing revealed F508del/3849 + 10kbC-T mutation, which is a common mutation associated with Cystic Fibrosis, and the patient's symptoms such as frequent respiratory episodes, uncertain sweat tests, and Pseudo-Bartter's syndrome are consistent with Cystic Fibrosis.

rejected.label: Pseudo-Bartter Syndrome
rejected.why: While the patient developed Pseudo-Bartter's syndrome, it is a known complication of Cystic Fibrosis, rather than a distinct diagnosis.

rejected.label: Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia
rejected.why: There is no mention of ciliary dysfunction or ultrastructural defects, which are characteristic of Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia.

rejected.label: Bronchiectasis
rejected.why: While the patient has respiratory episodes, there is no definitive evidence of bronchiectasis, and the lung computer tomography showed no signs of damage.

rejected.label: Shwachman-Diamond Syndrome
rejected.why: There is no mention of pancreatic insufficiency, neutropenia, or skeletal abnormalities, which are characteristic of Shwachman-Diamond Syndrome.
